display_title: Pay 2 Win: The World is Mine

reviews.text: Let’s talk gameplay: you lay back on your chair and enjoy money sounds. That’s it. You just put the stuff on the screen and you enjoy number triggers like it's a legit casino. You don’t even try hard to get your money. The game does that for you. Because apparently the developers saw how little effort gamers were putting into life and said, “Let’s meet them halfway.” It's like a bullet hell shooter got drunk and passed out on a CRT monitor from 1993, and somehow, it’s art. And oh, the dopamine. Every explosion, every shiny gem, every upgrade - it’s like your brain is getting suckled by an arcade machine from a timeline where Castlevania went completely feral. Level up every 7 seconds. The soundtrack? Banger. Absolute banger. I’ve started hearing Annie's and May's voices in the background while doing dishes. My dishwasher has a kill combo. I don’t even have a dishwasher. The characters? Oh, the deep, rich, emotionally resonant lore of “That blue girl” and “This blonde goddess.” There are approximately up to hundreds of different builds and they all boil down to: “Hits stuff good.” Thank God. If I wanted emotional arcs, I’d rewatch Breaking Bad. I’m here to place stuff on board while getting trillions of money in a single trigger like a Roomba with war crimes. And don’t get me started on the items. The Critkeeper? Yes, please, give me that crit so I can feel something. Cocktail Waitress? The game equivalent of putting the entire universe on hold while you decide whether to eat string cheese. The real star though? Roulette Wheel. You get that, and you become a god of shiny screens and start considering spending your whole life in casino. You ever walked into a room so pungent you're richer than Elon Musk himself? You will. And yet. And yet. I cannot stop. I am freebasing astonishing graphic design. I am optimizing builds in my sleep. I see XP level ups in my dreams. My mouse hand has calcified into a permanent claw, but my soul? My soul is radiant. Bathed in golden coins and the unholy light of multi-billion dollar re-triggers. 10/10. Highly recommend. Don’t do this to yourself.
Numbers go up and the sounds are good, you even get to choose between three things! Did another play through since 1.0 dropped, still good will go roulette wheel gambling again.

Has some potential, but it doesnt really seem worth the current price. Maybe this will change in the future but i doubt it, as the core gameplay loop isnt really engaging. Some systems are weird and make no sense, like rerolling link cost scaling with rarity. The gameplay isnt very deep, just adjust your board layout and choose which direction to navigate on the skill tree, that is all. 99% of gameplay is either rearranging the board or unlocking skill nodes. You can also sometimes cast spells. This often isnt even worth doing though as you have a 30% bonus to output if you are afk, and casting a spell removes the afk buff. Its like an idle game with almost no progression and no new unlocks after the first 10 minutes. There just isnt anything worth waiting for.

一个有着许多不同的流派打法的增量游戏，同流派组合可以质变，虽然刷连接点有点难受，但目前体验还是挺不错的。但是英语太烂玩的很累，如果有机会的话，希望可以加上中文翻译:) This is an incremental idle game featuring numerous distinct build archetypes; combining builds from the same archetype brings transformative power spikes. Farming connection nodes can get tedious, yet overall the gameplay is enjoyable so far. That said, my limited English makes playing quite draining, so I hope official Chinese translation will be added sometime down the line:)

Fun game, great voice acting, and a funny story. However, it gets stuck at a certain point where there's not much left to do. The cards you get from packs are usually the same as the latest pack you obtained. For example, if you choose Annie, about 80% of the cards you receive will be Annie cards. This makes it difficult to change your strategy later, since you're basically locked into a magic-focused build from that point on. This is my recommendation: the most enjoyable part of this game is being able to adjust my strategy whenever I get stuck. If the game forces players into a specific path, either directly or indirectly, it becomes boring very quickly. Since it's an incremental game, there isn't much else to do, so having the freedom to experiment with different tactics is what keeps it interesting. The unlocking floor plan system is actually one of the game's weaker features. I unlocked certain floor plans because they fit my strategy at the time, but later, when I obtained new facilities and wanted to change my layout, I couldn't. The new facilities couldn't connect properly with my existing floor plan, which forced me to keep using the same setup. A feature that allows players to sell, remove, or rebuild floor plans would greatly improve the game. It would give players the flexibility to adapt their strategy as they unlock new facilities instead of being permanently locked into earlier decisions.
Mechanics aren't especially interesting, writing is especially annoying.
It doesnt feel good. Its more of an afk game. I was expecting more active play.

Too much randomness locking you out of any real synergy between different components. Rerolling links does little to help and ends up wasting resources as each attempt gets more expensive. Upgrading crappy components is a waste of resources and there are too many components that are a waste of space. Unlocking tiles for a specific configuration of existing components and then drawing a new component that is useless under the current unlocked layout. I did get to the "ending" with my first run, but more than half of the components on my board were just taking up space to complete links. All of the things each of those components were meant to do was rendered meaningless without full access to every component from every pack. The only real upside to the game was the fun little story, but that didn't even feel worth all the effort by the end.

you place facilities on a grid to make your game studio produce money. most facilities don't directly produce money, but instead give buffs and power up adjacent facilities. the game is a puzzle to find and arrange facilities that work well together and make money as fast as possible. it's a bit like backpack battles, but without the pvp. you're accompanied by two anime girls - annie and may (very subtle.) may from accounting is focused on profitability, has a gambling problem, and recognizes that you can't make good games if your studio goes bankrupt. annie is a gaming boomer (somewhat disdainful of the modern state of gaming) and also a witch who's become a company VIP with their magic powers and elite gaming skills. they both have the same goal (make the studio succeed) but have opposing views on how it should be done, and their interactions are pretty entertaining and well written for an incremental game. you can auto-skip story dialogue and the game even asks on first play if you want to do so, but i'd recommend not skipping it. you level up as you earn money, giving you star coins which can be used to randomly pull a new facility or make progress on the skill tree. the gacha is quite fair - you can never pull a duplicate facility (except for facilities that allow more than one to be placed) and can pick from three options when you pull, but the star coin cost can be painful at times and there is a constant pressure of choosing whether to risk star coins on a pull or save them up to buy skill tree upgrades instead. facilities can be neutral or aligned with annie/may: annie facilities are about active play, stacking buffs and making big plays when your buffs are all synced up and active. may facilities are about idling, accumulating raw earning power, and gambling. you start off with eight neutral facilities and more facilities have to be unlocked via the skill tree. the order in which they're unlocked is also randomized - there are 11 packs of 6-9 facilities and you get one at random when you purchase a pack unlock. it can feel bad if you're focused on annie facilities, spend a bunch of coins to unlock a pack, and end up getting a pack with all may facilities or neutral facilities that don't help your build. it's possible to just hit nothing but bad outcomes when you're spending your star coins or spend your coins inefficiently and then feel stuck because the money requirements for more star coins keep scaling up but your money production hasn't. the game tries to protect you from this by periodically resetting missions that award star coins (i thought it was a glitch at first as there seems to be no indication that these missions are supposed to reset, and saving/reloading the game seems to make the reset happen faster). but that does mean you will sometimes have to just sit through a bad time, with no meaningful actions you can take, and wait for your handout of star coins. or close the game and come back to it later. if you're looking to actively play through the game and not idle through it, there's a small risk of playing yourself into a dead end or having the game just randomly force you into idle. aside from star coins, there's also the money that your studio is earning. this money is used to upgrade your facilities, reroll their links (placing facilities so that they're linked gives you an income multiplier), and expand your grid - you start off with just a 1x1 square and have to purchase more squares. i often found myself wanting to redo my layout but also feeling like the game was discouraging me from experimenting because my grid restricts where i can place facilities and now i'd have to spend a lot of money to reroll links (the cost scales up and it's almost always a significant amount of money). i get that there should be things you need to spend money on, but i also have to wonder if the game would just be more fun if you just started with the full 7x7 grid and had cheap link rerolls. the game is rather short, but there are multiple endings depending on which girl you side with. each ending also gives you a special facility which will carry over to new game+. new game+ resets everything, unlocks more of the skill tree, and gives you a special new game+ facility (the tesseract) plus all the ending facilities you've ever earned. this is enough of a power boost to make new game+ much smoother than your first playthrough. overall i've enjoyed my time with the game. the game could use a bit more polish but i've seen the developer be very active at taking and implementing feedback, so this will probably improve in the future.
Playing around with builds is super fun, finding things that are broken, resetting, and trying to find new broken things. It's the incremental I've been looking for all my life.
Lots of fun, seems like there are plenty of build options, fully voice acted and cute characters

Great game I very much enjoyed it. However I have one major issue with it that I feel people should be aware of which is the fact there is no autosave feature from what I see 6 hours in. To put it bluntly I lost about 6.4 hours of progress to that fact. Which because the game is fun and has a lot of different options I can move on from. But I imagine for others it would make or break the experience if you don't know or accidentally assume so and lost hours of progress like I did. I hope they add a autosave in the future and this review will definitely be adjusted if they do. But for now that's how I feel and that's how I feel and how things are.
Great game to play when you are watching streams or doing something else. Dev also responds to bugs and suggestions quickly.
Very cool game, loved cucking May.
After 2 hours the combo part was done. Let it simmer 3-4 more hours without touching and the game is suddenly over.

A fun idler with a bunch of options in terms of build choice that can be somewhat limited by what packs you get early, but in a game like this the RNG behind it doesn't feel too bad since you get them all eventually anyway and all it may do is slow you down a bit. Which for an idler means you leave the game open a bit longer, not a big deal. The story is amusing and if it isnt your thing you can just skip every scene and go through the routes to get its unlocks. Each girl has two permanent unlocks and then there's a neutral route as well. The devs are great as well, I had an issue with my save that wouldnt let me progress and despite it being a sunday they responded within a few hours and fixed the save and are working on a permanent fix to the issue, so thats also a big plus. All in all definitely worth playing if you have any interest in idlers as I've spent a surprising amount of time setting up stuff just right. it also has long term achievements, like getting vigintillion or 10^63 dollars.

Granted I haven't finished a run yet but for an incremental game where the focus on combos and structuring your facilities to get the best set up, it really hits a complete content wall block. From the start you progress quick enough where you are able to keep buying packs to get new units and also the skill tree with +1% nothings but when you run out and your luck is bad enough to give you units that don't stack well enough there's not much you can do other than just go to bed with your pc on. Most of the facilities I received are under the May section which is supposed to be idle which is fine but in my playthrough I only have gotten 2 annies to show up and even then they couldn't slot in to make a dent in the money objective. It wouldn't be that much of an issue but with the gameplay almost completely halted this is where I would've had the chance to prestige or do something else gameplay related to pick up the pace again to regain my interest.

I have seen the glory of God in low resolution and it changed my life! A very fun semi-idle game that encourages you to find broken combos, which I enjoy. Amazing voice acting too, and funny dialogue that I didn't want to skip. I appreciate the new game + mode too.

Relatively chill game that has a lot more mechanics than you actually need to progress or eventually win. It can look intimidating, but don’t be scared; numbers will go up even if you don’t min-max! And your first run will be your hardest before every one afterwards gets easier. Only critique is that unlocking the various endings is a bit opaque and it’s hard to continue replaying when I don’t know what to do differently to unlock everything. But for an idle/incremental game it’s a fun time. Bonus points for full voice acting and a story!

Great incremental game with nice idea, good execution and nice story. It is something little different than standard incremental games today, but that makes it even better, it works like a charm, beautifully done.

I enjoyed the game, but I feel like the progression can be slow at times. Pros: * The writing can be funny * I like the soundtrack. * It's satisfying watching the credits go up. Cons: * After a certain point, the progression starts slowing down a lot. * There's a tutorial, but after that you're left to figure things out on your own. * It takes a long time to unlock the ability to prestige, and depending on the build you ended up with, finishing a run can become a chore. Bugs: * The button to refund the upgrades doesn't work.

this game is great, if you like other games like it. this would be no ones jumping off point, thats for certain. other than that, i think the humor is really good, its fun, meta, absurd, every other buzzword to describe comedy now

this is a fun incremental, ironically not pay 2 win, the main problem I see is that the story content is arbitrarily locked and it is unclear what to do when you want the next story beat, is it money? level? morality?
great game

Pay 2 Win: The World Is Mine is entertaining for the first couple of hours, but it falls apart quickly after that. By around the 3 hour mark, the game is essentially over, with no more content left to explore. The big skill tree is probably the most disappointing part. It looks impressive on paper and gives the impression of depth and long playtime, but in practice it is just a facade. There is nowhere near as much actual content behind it as the size of the tree suggests. In short: fun start, but the game does not deliver on what it promises, and you will have seen everything long before you feel like you are actually done.

Pay 2 Win still needs a lot of work, and it's missing metrics you'd actually need to see which facilities are making you the most money. Kind of a big deal for a game about optimizing revenue. Achievements are bugged too. Too many bugs to recommend it seriously as is. Maybe worth another look if they patch it up.
